details: The brief decides "any run not judged ... makes the plugin-evals step fail". A run the ceiling stopped before it
started is a run not judged, but report() counts only runs that are present: it walks case["arms"] and never compares
with case["runsPerCase"] (every real case carries it, e.g. 3 in the guard-batch record), and data["partial"] only adds
a note. evals/judge-measure/tally.py, the project's other reader of the same --json, already treats both as NOT JUDGED
(tally.py:67 "the run is partial", tally.py:94 want_runs = runsPerCase), and its README says "a run stopped at the
ceiling is partial, so tally answers NOT JUDGED". Reachable: bin/ci passes --max-cost-usd (cap minus (jobs-1) x the
largest run) precisely so that the ceiling can trip, and a full batch costs about $8-9 against the default cap 15.
CONFIRMED for bin/eval-record (reproduced, outputs below). PLAUSIBLE end to end: whether claude plugin eval itself exits
non-zero on a ceiling stop is not known (no record of one in ~/.relay/evals; finding it out is a paid run). If it does
exit non-zero the step is red already, but the record line still says nothing is wrong.
evidence: $ python3 -I (fixture from tests/test_eval_record.py, rec.main on each)
partial, 1 of 3 runs: exit 0 |     note: partial run: cost ceiling reached
runsPerCase 3, 1 run present: exit 0 | ci: eval record: 0 meaning grader(s) failed, 0 split votes
case with 0 runs: exit 0 | ci: eval record: 0 meaning grader(s) failed, 0 split votes
failing_case: A record with "partial": true, "partialReason": "cost ceiling reached" and a case whose runsPerCase is 3 but holds
1 judged passing run: bin/eval-record exits 0, last line "    note: partial run: cost ceiling reached".
The same record with partial false and runsPerCase 3 / 1 run, and a case with runsPerCase 3 and 0 runs: both exit 0,
last line "ci: eval record: 0 meaning grader(s) failed, 0 split votes".
If claude plugin eval exits 0 on a ceiling stop, bin/ci then ends "ci: green" with 2 of 3 runs never judged.
Should: exit 2 with the NOT A PASS line naming the case (2 not judged), as the project's own tally.py does.
fix_hint: In report(): for each case, count max(0, runsPerCase - len(runs)) per arm as not judged (add the case to bad, one note
"N of M runs missing"); when data["partial"] is true, count it as not a pass too (e.g. unjudged at least 1, or a
separate "partial" reason in the NOT A PASS line). Tests in tests/test_gate_not_judged.py.
pass_cases: 1. fixture([[True]*3], partial="cost ceiling reached") with runsPerCase 3: main() returns 2; the last line starts
"ci: eval record: NOT A PASS" and names code-reviewer-offbyone.
2. fixture([[True]*3]) with runsPerCase 3 (1 run present), partial false: returns 2, "2 not judged".
3. fixture([[True]*3]*3) with runsPerCase 3, partial false: returns 0, no "NOT A PASS" (today's green case).
4. The stored record 2026-10-24T04-41-52Z-wt-archive-inert.json (15 cases x 3 runs, partial false): still returns 0.
reason: tests/test_gate_not_judged.py:50,58,63,68 (partial, fewer runs, no runs) pass and fail on old code; :73 keeps green case.
findings.summary: a batch stopped at the cost ceiling (partial) or a case with fewer runs than runsPerCase exits 0, so runs that never ran are not counted as not judged

details: PLAUSIBLE: today claude writes the file whenever it exits 0 in every stored run, and a non-zero claude exit already
makes the step red, so this needs claude to exit 0 without a record. Under the brief's rule (nothing judged is not a
pass) "no record" is the extreme of "not judged"; the docstring keeps exit 0 on purpose, from before the change.
Cheap to fix with the same exit 2. Size: 5 agent minutes.

failing_case: bin/ci deletes .ci/evals.json, then claude plugin eval exits 0 without writing --json (a tool change, a crash after

"ci: green" with nothing judged. Should: exit 2 (not a pass: no record).
